deep_join.note: How each genomic deep past meets its anchor (ToLaD#143, replacing #77/#80/#71): the genome gives the shape, the anchor the number. The whole genomic curve is scaled by one factor so its young end (pre-modern) meets the higher of the first cited count (a history file's baseline or first point, any year) and the modelled natural level: the count when it is the higher (`next` cited), else the natural level in 1500 CE, from which the range-loss trend runs down to the count (`next` natural); with no cited count, the modelled level (the natural level in 1500 CE, the natural baseline, today's modelled count; `next` modelled). It is held flat to it. ratio = genomic level at its young end / anchor, before scaling; flagged when beyond 10x either way; factor = 1 / ratio, except on a flagged join whose young end is below the median of its resolved steps (ToLaD#172, `meet` median): that median meets the anchor instead (factor = anchor / res_median_raw) and the young steps it puts below the anchor are held at it (`held`), so the deep past peaks at most res_max_raw / res_median_raw above the anchor; not where [deep.blind] cites the young end's decline (the lion).
